close_reason: Container tier green on arm64: 988 passed in 659s (full suite, integration included), with the browser image building FROM node:<tag>@sha256:<index digest> on arm64 -- which is the real proof the index digest resolves per-architecture rather than to a single-arch child. Guard verified behaviourally, not just by string assertion: docker image inspect on the rendered pandoc reference exits 0, the same reference with one hex digit changed exits non-zero, and the OLD probe (docker images -q) is blind to the present reference. amd64 is covered by CI at the PR gate.

title: Document the bump, the veraPDF fact, and cut 0.39.0
description:
Files: AGENTS.md, stencil/assets/README.md, CHANGELOG.md, stencil/__init__.py

AGENTS.md, in 'Every version the scaffolding installs lives in pipeline.py':
- Bumping an image is two steps -- edit the tag in IMAGE_TAGS, then 'python3 scripts/resolve_image_digests.py' -- stated beside the existing lockfile re-vendor step, in the same shape.
- Say why the digest is KEYED by the tag rather than inlined: a registry resolves name:tag@digest BY THE DIGEST and ignores the tag, so an inline pair whose tag moved without a re-resolve silently builds the old image, while a keyed one cannot be expressed and fails when the constant is read.
- FIX THE STALE CLOSING SENTENCE of that section: 'The images are still pinned by mutable tag rather than by digest, for all three of them -- stn-8vi.' That becomes false the moment this lands. Nothing tests prose.
- Document the ensure_image probe change: 'docker images -q' cannot see a digest-pinned reference (measured), so the guard became 'docker image inspect', which additionally verifies the digest rather than only the name. This changes what a GENERATED PACKAGE does, not just what stencil pins, so it belongs in the written record rather than only in a commit message.
- Record the veraPDF fact: verapdf/cli:v1.30.2 is a single-arch (linux/amd64) manifest, not a manifest list, so its pin is an image digest and it already runs emulated on arm64.

stencil/assets/README.md: a third section for image-digests.json, following the two already there. FIX THE LEAD -- the file opens 'Two kinds of artifact live here', which a third section contradicts on line 3. Note that unlike the two lockfiles this file is NOT shipped into a generated package; it is stencil's own build metadata, and what a package receives is the resolved tag@digest string already rendered into its compose file, Dockerfile and Makefile.

CHANGELOG.md: new '## 0.39.0' section at the TOP (the operator consolidates the batch's versions at landing, so a conflict here is expected and not ours to resolve). Carry the veraPDF finding and the ensure_image probe change, both with their measurements.

stencil/__init__.py: __version__ = '0.39.0'.

The recovery path is 'a pull failing with manifest unknown means the digest was garbage-collected -- re-resolve and regenerate'. AGENTS.md already records the same regret about Chromium; this must not reproduce it silently.

NOT DONE HERE, mention in the PR rather than filing (neither is a defect): an arm64 CI leg (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm) would make the multi-arch claim something CI holds rather than a one-time human run, and CI pre-pulls pandoc and node but not veraPDF though the stated reason applies identically. title: Implement: ensure_image probe must see a digest-pinned image
description:
Files: stencil/templates/Makefile-base.j2

MEASURED: 'docker images -q docker.io/library/node:24.20.0-alpine3.24@sha256:e675...' prints nothing even though the image is present locally, while the same probe with the bare tag prints the id. So the current guard, 'docker images -q $(1) | grep -q . || $(DC) pull $(2)', can never succeed once a digest is pinned, and every make doc / make pdf / make format-md pulls again. 'docker image inspect <ref>' answers correctly, and reports ABSENT for a wrong digest -- which is what the guard always claimed to do but could not, since a bare-tag probe passes while compose fetches something else.

POSIX branch:  @docker image inspect $(1) >/dev/null 2>&1 || $(DC) pull $(2)
Windows branch: keep the powershell wrapper; escape make's $ as $$ for $null and $LASTEXITCODE. BOTH BRANCHES MUST CHANGE -- the old assertion was one substring common to both, so changing only the POSIX arm leaves Windows consumers pulling on every build with a green suite.

ALSO FIX THE RUNTIME THE PROBE NAMES. Both reviewers flagged that ensure_image hardcodes 'docker' while DC ?= docker compose is advertised on line 2 as overridable to 'podman compose'. On a podman-only host the probe has ALWAYS failed and the guard has always been an unconditional pull. MEASURED: podman images -q DOES see a digest-pinned ref (exit 0) where docker images -q does not, so the headline measurement is docker-specific too.
    CONTAINER ?= $(firstword $(subst -, ,$(DC)))
The subst is what makes this never worse than today: 'docker-compose' becomes two words so firstword yields 'docker', 'podman-compose' yields 'podman', and 'docker compose'/'podman compose' already yield the right word. All four spellings pipeline.compose_command() falls through now probe with a binary that exists. Plain $(firstword $(DC)) would have broken the two standalone binaries, which have no 'image inspect' -- that is why the subst is there and not decoration.

QUOTE THE REFERENCE in both branches -- 'docker image inspect '$(1)'' on POSIX and quoted inside the PowerShell string. The ref is now partly machine-derived; word-splitting and PowerShell's $/backtick handling are free to close.

COMMENT-WORTHY: image inspect ignores the tag when a digest is present (MEASURED on both runtimes: hello-world:BOGUSTAG@<correct digest> exits 0). Same rule as the registry's, which is this epic's whole argument for keying by tag -- so the probe is consistent, but do not let a reader think it validates the tag.

This whole task is collateral the ticket did not name. Say so in the commit message that carries it, WITH the measurement, so git blame does not read it as a drive-by.

Acceptance: tests/test_pipeline.py::test_the_makefile_checks_for_the_image_compose_actually_runs passes against the new probe in both branches; the rendered Makefile still names the same reference compose runs.
close_reason: ensure_image now probes 'image inspect' via $(CONTAINER) (derived from $(DC) with the documented subst/firstword), quoted reference, both OS arms fixed (POSIX + PowerShell $null/$LASTEXITCODE). Verified in an isolated copy (HEAD pipeline.py + this file only, since the shared worktree's pipeline.py is mid-flight on a sibling task): tests/test_pipeline.py::test_the_makefile_checks_for_the_image_compose_actually_runs PASSES; make -n doc OS=Darwin/Windows_NT both exit 0 with correct 'docker image inspect <pinned-ref>' lines; no 'docker images -q' remains. See comment for the git-reset incident that hit the shared worktree mid-session and the current VendoredAssetError blocker (sibling's image-digests.json not yet vendored) that is out of this task's file scope.

title: Implement: IMAGE_TAGS, pinned_image and the lazy image constants
description:
Make the pipeline half of the red tests pass.

Files: stencil/pipeline.py ONLY.

BOOTSTRAP CONSTRAINT -- this is why the design is not the obvious one. pinned_image() raises on a tag with no recorded digest. If the three *_IMAGE constants were computed at module level, then the moment a maintainer bumps a tag, 'import stencil.pipeline' raises -- which is the exact moment scripts/resolve_image_digests.py and scripts/vendor_npm_locks.py (which does 'from stencil import pipeline') need to import it. The documented bump procedure would deadlock on its own import on the first bump after this lands. Confirmed by construction, not assumed.

THE FIX (verified): PEP 562 module __getattr__.
- IMAGE_TAGS = {'node': ..., 'pandoc': ..., 'verapdf': ...} -- plain strings, eager, always readable.
- NODE_TAG / PANDOC_TAG / VERAPDF_TAG read from IMAGE_TAGS, eager.
- pinned_image(tag) -> '<tag>@sha256:...' by lookup in stencil/assets/image-digests.json, read lazily through lru_cache (the shape stencil/assets.py already uses for vendored artifacts). Unknown tag raises with a message naming the tag and scripts/resolve_image_digests.py.
- module-level __getattr__ resolves NODE_IMAGE / PANDOC_IMAGE / VERAPDF_IMAGE on attribute access; __dir__ lists them so dir(pipeline) and tab-completion still show them.
Verified that this keeps working: pipeline.NODE_IMAGE, from stencil import pipeline, from stencil.pipeline import PANDOC_IMAGE, and CI's python -c. So generate.py, every template, .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/vendor_npm_locks.py stay untouched -- that is the point.

COMMENTS. Rewrite the 'A TAG, NOT A DIGEST -- deliberately' block at pipeline.py:86-97: it is the argument this epic overturns and it points at stn-8vi as the open question. Add the veraPDF fact at VERAPDF_IMAGE: verapdf/cli:v1.30.2 is a single application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json, linux/amd64 only -- there is no manifest list, so its pin is an image digest, and it already runs emulated on arm64. Correct the source ticket's manifest-list assumption rather than repeating it. Also say why the digest is KEYED by the tag rather than inlined as one string: a registry resolves name:tag@digest BY THE DIGEST and ignores the tag, so an inline pair whose tag moved without a re-resolve silently builds the old image.

Acceptance: the unknown-tag and tags-readable tests pass. The digest-form and key-set tests STAY RED until stn-e72.6 produces stencil/assets/image-digests.json -- this task must not hand-write that file. The Makefile-probe test STAYS RED until stn-e72.3 lands -- do NOT edit stencil/templates/Makefile-base.j2 from this task. Whole-suite green is stn-e72.5.

THE COST BEING ACCEPTED -- a paragraph in the pipeline.py comment, in the same shape as the lockfile's 'THE COST BEING ACCEPTED' block, so nobody later 'fixes' this by going back to a tag. A digest pin gives a CONSUMER three new ways to fail that a tag pin did not:
  1. Registry GC. A tag pin degrades to different bytes; a digest pin degrades to 'manifest unknown'. Once upstream repushes the tag the old manifest is untagged, and untagged manifests do get reclaimed -- so the pin has an expiry date the tag did not.
  2. docker save -> transfer -> docker load -> docker tag loses RepoDigests, so both 'image inspect ...@sha256:...' and the compose pull fail against a reference that worked as a tag. A pull-through cache preserves digests; a save/load air-gap does not.
  3. No override. generate.py's reject_derived deliberately refuses template_env: {pandoc_image: ...}, so a consumer behind a mirror has no supported knob and hand-editing the generated Makefile is undone by the next stencil gen.
Deliberately NO escape hatch: rendering through overridable variables would need Makefile-doc.j2, Makefile-pkg.j2 and docker-compose-html.yml.j2 -- all outside this epic's approved boundary -- and would let an environment variable downgrade the very pin this exists to create. What is written down instead is the RECOVERY PATH: a pull failing with 'manifest unknown' means the digest was garbage-collected; re-resolve with scripts/resolve_image_digests.py and regenerate. AGENTS.md already records this exact regret about Chromium ('neither the Makefile nor the compose file gives a consumer a build argument to work around it with'); do not reproduce it silently on three more images.

ALSO IN THE VERAPDF COMMENT: with a tag, a future multi-arch repush of v1.30.2 would silently start running native on arm64; with a digest it stays emulated until someone re-resolves. That freeze is the point of the pin -- say it, so it is not rediscovered as a bug.
close_reason: Implemented IMAGE_TAGS, pinned_image(), and lazy NODE_IMAGE/PANDOC_IMAGE/VERAPDF_IMAGE via PEP 562 module __getattr__/__dir__ in stencil/pipeline.py (only file touched). test_a_tag_with_no_recorded_digest_fails_loudly and test_the_tags_are_readable_without_resolving_them now pass. The 7 tests required to stay red (digest-form/key-set/probe tests pending stn-e72.3 and stn-e72.6) remain red, for the right reason (missing stencil/assets/image-digests.json, not hand-written per instructions). Manual checks confirmed: pipeline.IMAGE_TAGS reads plain tags eagerly; pipeline.NODE_IMAGE raises VendoredAssetError naming scripts/resolve_image_digests.py; 'NODE_IMAGE' in dir(pipeline) is True. Rewrote the NODE_IMAGE 'A TAG NOT A DIGEST' comment block, added the veraPDF single-arch-manifest fact and freeze rationale at VERAPDF_TAG, and added a THE COST BEING ACCEPTED paragraph (registry GC, save/load losing RepoDigests, no override + recovery path) in the same shape as the BROWSER_LOCKFILE comment. Whole-suite collateral: many doc_package-fixture tests now error/fail because image-digests.json does not exist yet -- expected per the epic ('Whole-suite green is stn-e72.5'), verified against baseline (543 passed pre-change vs 330 post-change, all new failures traced to the same missing-JSON VendoredAssetError). Filed stn-rf2 (discovered-from, not parented) for an unrelated environment issue found mid-task: Makefile-base.j2 was modified in this worktree by what appears to be a concurrent stn-e72.3 agent sharing the same working directory.

title: Write tests: digest-pinned images (red)
description:
Write the failing tests for stn-8vi. TDD red phase.

Files: tests/test_pins.py, tests/test_pipeline.py

New in tests/test_pins.py:
- test_every_image_the_scaffolding_pulls_is_pinned_by_digest: over the rendered doc package, every compose service without a 'build' key, every FROM in Dockerfile.browser, and every ensure_image call site names <repo>:<tag>@sha256:<64 hex>.
- test_the_pinned_digests_cover_the_architectures_we_build_on: node and pandoc record an INDEX media type and both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 in stencil/assets/image-digests.json; verapdf is allowed its single-arch manifest.v2 and is named explicitly, so a future multi-arch release is a deliberate edit rather than a silent pass.
- test_the_recorded_digests_are_exactly_the_tags_the_scaffolding_pins: set(json keys) == set(pipeline.IMAGE_TAGS.values()). WHY: platforms and media_type are RECORDS, not re-checkable facts, so 'the file is exactly what the script produced from the current tags' is the only thing holding them honest. Catches a hand-edited JSON, an entry for a tag that was bumped away, and an entry the resolver never wrote. Message names scripts/resolve_image_digests.py.
- test_a_tag_with_no_recorded_digest_fails_loudly: pipeline.pinned_image() on an unknown tag raises and the message names scripts/resolve_image_digests.py.
- test_the_tags_are_readable_without_resolving_them: pipeline.IMAGE_TAGS is reachable on a module whose digest file has no entry for one of its tags. This is the regression guard for the bootstrap deadlock (see stn-e72.2); without it, the first person to 'simplify' the lazy attribute access reintroduces it.

Amend (each breaks on a digest suffix or asserts the old probe):
- tests/test_pins.py::test_the_scaffolding_names_one_node_image_and_it_is_pinned -- rpartition(':') now yields the digest hex. SPLIT ON '@' FIRST, then take the tag.
- tests/test_pins.py::test_every_image_the_scaffolding_pulls_carries_a_version_tag -- same. The surviving delta from the new digest test is the 'tag contains a digit' check that catches lts-alpine, and it MUST run against the tag: a 64-char hex digest satisfies any(c.isdigit()) essentially always, so without the split this amendment passes vacuously. This is the amendment most likely to be made green rather than made correct.
- tests/test_pipeline.py::test_the_pandoc_image_is_pinned -- rpartition(':').
- tests/test_pipeline.py::test_the_makefile_checks_for_the_image_compose_actually_runs -- asserts the literal 'docker images -q $(1)'. The replacement must assert the probe in the WINDOWS branch and the POSIX branch SEPARATELY: the old assertion was a single substring present in both arms of the ifeq($(OS),Windows_NT) block, so a change to only the POSIX line would leave every Windows consumer pulling on every build with a green suite. tests/test_package_sources.py (around line 226) already tests both branches; follow that pattern.

RED/GREEN ACCEPTANCE -- READ THIS, IT IS THE HIGHEST-SILENCE TRAP IN THE EPIC.
Of the four amendments, only TWO go red on their own:
  - test_the_scaffolding_names_one_node_image_and_it_is_pinned (re.fullmatch of the version pattern against 64 hex chars)
  - test_pipeline.py::test_the_pandoc_image_is_pinned (same, against its own pattern)
The other TWO are SILENT REGRESSIONS that stay green while checking nothing:
  - test_every_image_the_scaffolding_pulls_carries_a_version_tag: rpartition(':')[2] yields the digest hex, and hex contains digits, so any(c.isdigit()) passes. ':' in image also passes. If this amendment is skipped because the bar is green, stencil PERMANENTLY loses its floating-tag guard -- 'docker.io/pandoc/core:latest@sha256:...' would satisfy it forever.
  - test_the_makefile_checks_for_the_image_compose_actually_runs: the literal 'docker images -q $(1)' appears in BOTH arms of the ifeq($(OS),Windows_NT) block, so swapping it for the new POSIX spelling is satisfied by editing only the POSIX line, leaving every Windows consumer pulling on every build.
Both must be rewritten anyway. For the probe test add the NEGATIVE assertion, which is what makes it un-skippable:
    assert "docker images -q" not in makefile, "a branch still uses the probe that cannot see a digest"

Acceptance: tests collect; the five new tests and the two genuinely-red amendments FAIL for the right reason (no pinned_image, no IMAGE_TAGS, no digest in the constants, no image-digests.json); the two silent amendments are rewritten and their new form fails too. Do NOT edit stencil/ or scripts/ from this task.

Confirmed both silent-regression amendments now fail non-vacuously (digest-format assertion catches the missing digest; negative 'docker images -q not in makefile' assertion catches the still-floating probe). 9 failed, 40 passed, 4 deselected (integration) in tests/test_pins.py + tests/test_pipeline.py under 'not integration'. Whole-suite collection unaffected (552/988 collected, 436 deselected).

title: Release bookkeeping: 0.39.0 CHANGELOG and version
description:
Files: CHANGELOG.md, stencil/__init__.py, .beads/issues.jsonl

- New "## 0.39.0" section at the TOP of CHANGELOG.md.

- STATE THE THREAT HONESTLY. Do not claim the pinned tree is now "the only tree that can
  run" full stop. What a consumer gets: an INCIDENTAL node_modules in the package
  directory -- someone, or some tool, ran npm install there -- can no longer silently
  drive make pdf with an unpinned puppeteer or pdf-lib. A hostile /workspace is NOT
  closed and is not closeable from inside the mount, since html-to-pdf.js is itself in
  the mount. Say that plainly; the wrong sentence here becomes a durable false belief.

- THE ENTRY MUST WARN CONSUMERS WHO OVERRIDE THE TEMPLATE. html-to-pdf.js.j2 is on the
  template search path; a project that has copied it into its own templates_dir keeps the
  vulnerable version and gets NO signal, because StrictUndefined cannot tell them -- a
  copy reads none of these keys. docker-compose-html.yml.j2's contract comment sets the
  precedent: say it in the release notes instead. Tell them to re-apply the change.

- NOTE THAT THE FIX DOES NOT REACH A PACKAGE UNTIL SOMEONE RUNS `stencil gen`.
  `make pkg` has no `gen` prerequisite (Makefile-pkg.j2), so an existing package keeps
  running its already-generated html-to-pdf.js until it is regenerated.

- stencil/__init__.py: __version__ = "0.39.0". Minor bump is correct per AGENTS.md --
  this changes what a generated package contains. The operator consolidates the batch's
  versions at landing, so a conflict here is expected and is not ours to resolve.

- BEFORE THE FINAL COMMIT, run: bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl, and commit it.
  Per AGENTS.md the pre-push hook refuses the push when the database and the export
  disagree, and it checks the export IN THE REVISION BEING PUSHED -- exporting without
  committing leaves the push failing. Note that the working tree already carries
  pre-existing drift in .beads/*.jsonl from ordinary bd reads.

Acceptance: stencil version prints 0.39.0; the 0.39.0 section is at the top of the
CHANGELOG, states the threat honestly, carries the template-override warning and the
"run stencil gen" note; .beads/issues.jsonl is committed.
close_reason: 0.39.0 CHANGELOG section written at the top, stating the threat honestly (closes an incidental node_modules; does NOT close a hostile /workspace, since html-to-pdf.js is itself in the mount), warning consumers who override html-to-pdf.js.j2 in their own templates_dir that they keep the old resolution and get no signal, and noting that make pkg has no gen prerequisite so the fix reaches a package only on the next stencil gen. __version__ bumped to 0.39.0; 'stencil version' prints 'stencil 0.39.0'. Export committed.

title: Implement: root html-to-pdf.js's requires at the tools directory
description:
Make the pinned tree the only tree html-to-pdf.js can run.

Files: stencil/templates/html-to-pdf.js.j2 (only)

=== THE CHANGE ===
    const { createRequire } = require("node:module");
    const fs = require("node:fs");            // keep the existing fs require; node: prefix optional but documents intent
    <argv usage check stays where it is>
    <the guard, see below>
    const fromTools = createRequire("{{ browser_tools_dir }}/package.json");
    const puppeteer = fromTools("puppeteer");
    const { PDFDocument, PDFName, ... } = fromTools("pdf-lib");

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, in this order:
  1. the existing input/output argv usage check (exit 2) stays FIRST -- otherwise
     `node html-to-pdf.js` with no arguments on a laptop reports the wrong problem
  2. the guard
  3. the two fromTools calls
Put the guard below the fromTools calls and it is dead code that can never fire.

TWO DIFFERENT CONTEXT KEYS, ON PURPOSE:
- createRequire base:  {{ browser_tools_dir }}/package.json   -- the RESOLUTION BASE, the
  install root npm ci is rooted at. The file exists (Dockerfile.browser printf's the
  manifest there).
- guard comparison:    {{ browser_node_modules }}             -- already a context key
  (generate.py:590), already rendered into NODE_PATH by Dockerfile.browser. Do NOT
  hand-concatenate {{ browser_tools_dir }}/node_modules. Under StrictUndefined a guessed
  key name is a hard stencil gen failure.

WHY createRequire AND NOT require('/opt/tools/node_modules/puppeteer'): requiring an
absolute DIRECTORY goes through Node's LOAD_AS_DIRECTORY, which reads package.json "main"
and IGNORES the "exports" field; a bare specifier resolved from a pinned base goes through
the full package resolution algorithm and honours exports. Measured at 8e17d65: they agree
today for both packages (puppeteer's exports["."].require and its main are the same file;
pdf-lib declares no exports), so the change is entry-point neutral right now. They stop
agreeing the first time a bump ships an exports map that diverges from main, and that
divergence would be silent. Put that reasoning in the comment.

Add one more sentence to that comment: the live future risk is a puppeteer bump that drops
the CJS "require" condition from its exports map -- on Node 24.20 require(esm) succeeds but
hands back a namespace, so the binding would silently become a module namespace object
instead of the module. AGENTS.md already requires a container-tier run when a pin moves,
and stn-cnm.1's acceptance test is what fails.

=== THE GUARD: CHECK IDENTITY, NOT EXISTENCE ===
Assert that resolution actually LANDS in the tools tree:

    fromTools.resolve("puppeteer").startsWith("{{ browser_node_modules }}")

NOT fs.existsSync. existsSync passes on an EMPTY /opt/tools/node_modules and on anything
mounted over it; the resolve check subsumes the existence check, is the same line count,
and is the assertion actually wanted. It also survives a future exports-map change, which
is the whole reason createRequire was chosen over a literal absolute path.

Wrap it so a MODULE_NOT_FOUND from resolve() becomes the same message rather than a raw
stack -- that is the not-in-the-image case and it must read as one.

THE MESSAGE MUST COVER BOTH REACHABLE CASES, because there are two, not one:
  (a) the script is being run outside the generated browser image (someone ran
      `node html-to-pdf.js` on their laptop);
  (b) html-to-pdf.js.j2 and Dockerfile.browser.j2 are BOTH on the template search path,
      and AGENTS.md documents that consumers override templates -- so a consumer who
      overrode Dockerfile.browser.j2 to install elsewhere while inheriting stencil's
      html-to-pdf.js.j2 is INSIDE the container and must not be told they are not.
Word it as: either this is not running inside the generated browser image, or
Dockerfile.browser installed the tools somewhere other than <dir>. Name the directory via
the template variable, never a literal.

Exit code 2, matching the usage-error path above it. Route it through the same
console.error shape as the .catch() at the bottom of the file, so the failure output is
one format rather than two.

A package missing INSIDE a tools tree that otherwise resolves still surfaces a raw
MODULE_NOT_FOUND: that is a broken image, and the raw error already names the package.

=== STATE THE THREAT HONESTLY IN THE COMMENT ===
Do not write that this makes the pinned tree "the only tree that can run" full stop.
html-to-pdf.js is ITSELF in the mount, as are the Makefile, docker-compose.yml,
Dockerfile.browser and the Lua filters, and `make pkg` has no `gen` prerequisite -- anyone
who can write /workspace/node_modules can equally write /workspace/html-to-pdf.js. What
this change closes:
  - CLOSED: an INCIDENTAL node_modules (someone, or some tool, ran npm install in the
    package directory) silently outranking the pinned tree. The real, common, traceless case.
  - CLOSED: a malicious package that arrived via an unrelated npm install there.
  - NOT CLOSED, and not closeable from inside the mount: a hostile /workspace.
Also note in the comment that a bare require here is a defect and why, so the next
generated script does not reinstate it -- NODE_PATH still makes a bare require WORK for
anyone testing outside a polluted workspace, which is how this would come back.

=== DO NOT TOUCH ===
window.__mermaidReady, the failed-asset refusal, page.pdf() options, the puppeteer.launch
call and its executablePath, NODE_PATH/PATH in Dockerfile.browser.j2, stencil/pipeline.py,
stencil/generate.py, tests/test_pipeline.py. Do NOT switch puppeteer to puppeteer-core in
this task -- that is stn-jeq and needs an operator decision.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- Every test from stn-cnm.1 passes, AND the container tier ACTUALLY RAN.
  conftest.py:211 SKIPS integration tests when no runtime is found, so a bare pytest is
  green on a machine without docker. AGENTS.md names this exact failure: "a tier that
  silently stops running is the failure mode this repository already learned from its
  pre-push hook".
  Run: pytest tests/test_pins.py -m integration
  REPORT THE COLLECTED AND PASSED COUNTS. A skip is a FAILED acceptance, not a pass.
- pytest -m 'not integration' stays green; no other test regresses.

Ordering: argv usage check, then guard, then the two fromTools() calls. title: Write tests: html-to-pdf.js resolves only from the pinned tools tree
description:
Write the tests FIRST; the fast-tier assertions and the acceptance test must fail against
today's bare requires.

Files: tests/test_pins.py (only)

=== FAST TIER (no container) ===
Beside test_the_browser_image_installs_from_the_pinned_manifest_and_lockfile:

1. Assert the rendered html-to-pdf.js roots module resolution at
   pipeline.BROWSER_TOOLS_DIR (assert against the CONSTANT, not a copy of the literal,
   the way the neighbouring Dockerfile assertions do).

2. Assert no generated .js does a BARE require of any pinned package. ITERATE
   pipeline.BROWSER_NPM_PINS -- do NOT hardcode the two names puppeteer and pdf-lib. A
   pin added tomorrow must be covered automatically; that is the same property-not-a-list
   shape test_nothing_in_the_scaffolding_installs_by_name already uses in this file.
   Scan every generated .js file, not only html-to-pdf.js.

   RUN THAT SCAN OVER code_lines(doc_package), NOT OVER read_text(). code_lines is already
   in this file (test_pins.py:112) and strips // comments; its docstring says "// covers
   html-to-pdf.js". stn-cnm.2 is required to write a comment EXPLAINING why a bare require
   is a defect here -- a raw-text scan fails on that comment, which is the exact trap that
   docstring was written for.

   Match the require CALL, e.g. require("<name>"), not any mention of the name: the guard
   in stn-cnm.2 legitimately contains fromTools.resolve("puppeteer").

=== CONTAINER TIER (pytest.mark.integration), beside the 'installed' fixture ===

WHERE THE IMAGE COMES FROM. pipeline.browser_image_tag() only returns a tag string; it
builds nothing. The pdf_workspace fixture (tests/conftest.py:335) is the ONLY thing in
the suite that calls pipeline.build_browser_image. tests/test_pins.py sorts before
tests/test_pdf.py, so a test that does not request pdf_workspace can be the first
integration test to run and will hit a tag that does not exist.

So: REQUEST pdf_workspace -- for the built image and the rendered page -- but MOUNT YOUR
OWN tmp dir. Recipe, session-scoped so the cost is paid once:
  1. pipeline.render("doc", "document.md", "document.html", workdir=pdf_workspace),
     exactly as the 'installed' fixture does at test_pins.py:809.
  2. Copy document.html and html-to-pdf.js out of pdf_workspace into your own tmp dir.
     Generated pages are self-contained (assets inlined at gen time), so two files render.
  3. Plant node_modules/puppeteer and node_modules/pdf-lib decoys in that tmp dir.
  4. Pass workdir=<that tmp dir> to pipeline.html_to_pdf / pipeline.run_in_browser.

NEVER plant decoys in pdf_workspace itself. The 'installed' fixture's PROBE script opens
with a bare require("pa11y"), so a decoy there would corrupt the pinned-tree assertions
themselves, not merely test_pdf.py's geometry.

DECOY SHAPE, and it is load-bearing. Each decoy is a directory with a package.json
carrying a wrong marker version AND a main/index.js whose MODULE BODY throws a
distinctive marker string -- thrown at require time, not on first call. If a decoy is
malformed enough that Node cannot load it as a package (no main, no index.js), Node does
not error: it CONTINUES the resolution loop to the next directory and lands on NODE_PATH.
The acceptance test would then pass vacuously against unfixed code.

TEST 1 -- ACCEPTANCE. Run pipeline.html_to_pdf(workdir=<tmp dir>): same image, same
mount, same entrypoint as the compose pdf service. Assert exit 0, a PDF on disk, and the
marker string absent from stderr.

TEST 2 -- CONTROL, and it must assert the right half. The acceptance test's load-bearing
assertion is exit 0; "marker absent from stderr" is vacuous unless something proves the
decoy WOULD have produced that marker. So the control must, via pipeline.run_in_browser
in the same directory, do try { require("puppeteer") } catch and assert the MARKER STRING
comes back -- and the same for pdf-lib BY NAME. require.resolve naming the /workspace path
in addition, not instead.

pdf-lib needs that control specifically: both decoys throw at module load and the
puppeteer require comes first, so in the red state the script dies on puppeteer and never
reaches pdf-lib. pdf-lib is the more damaging hijack (it writes the PDF/UA role map that
make check-pdf exists to require), so its coverage rests entirely on this control.

PUT THE REAL RATIONALE IN THE CONTROL'S DOCSTRING, not "in case someone deletes the
fixture". The real one: a decoy Node cannot resolve as a package is SKIPPED rather than
errored, so a fixture an implementer plausibly gets wrong on the first try makes the
acceptance test pass vacuously against unfixed code.

TEST 3 -- THE GUARD MUST BE PROVEN TO FIRE. AGENTS.md is explicit that a guard which
silently does not run is worse than no guard (tests/test_export_drift.py exists because
of it), and nothing else here would notice if stn-cnm.2's guard were deleted. Run the
generated html-to-pdf.js under pipeline.NODE_IMAGE -- the plain node base image, which has
no /opt/tools -- with the same mount, and assert a non-zero exit AND that the message
names pipeline.BROWSER_TOOLS_DIR. One container invocation; builds no second image.

Reuse the already-built image elsewhere; do not build a second one. Bind no host port.

Acceptance: the fast-tier assertions and TEST 1 and TEST 3 FAIL (TDD red). TEST 2 PASSES
already -- that is what makes it a control.

Container tier: test_html_to_pdf_ignores_a_decoy_in_the_workspace (acceptance) and test_the_missing_tools_guard_names_the_pinned_dir (guard) fail; test_a_workspace_decoy_would_win_a_bare_require (control) passes. No other test in the suite regressed (fast tier: 547 passed / 2 new failures; integration tier for test_pins.py: 5 pre-existing passed / 2 new failures). Implementation is stn-cnm.2.

title: A non-string output_dir reaches the terminal as a TypeError traceback
description:
`_main` computes `output_base = (config_dir / output_dir_raw).resolve()` BEFORE the `package_contexts` pre-flight runs, so a config with a non-string `output_dir` (e.g. `output_dir: 7`) raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'PosixPath' and 'int'` as a bare traceback on every command that reaches that line -- gen, clean, and the branches below it.

Reproduced against 0.38.0 (worktree at 8e17d65):

    # .config.yaml
    output_dir: 7
    templates:
      - src: Makefile.j2
    packages:
      demo:
        package_type: none

    $ stencil clean --all
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      ...
      File "stencil/generate.py", line 1808, in _main
        output_base = (config_dir / output_dir_raw).resolve() if output_dir_raw else config_dir
    TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'PosixPath' and 'int'

`package_contexts` already classifies this as a config problem -- tests/test_config_fail_closed.py::test_a_non_string_output_dir_raises_valueerror_not_typeerror pins the ValueError at the unit level -- but the CLI never gets there, because output_base is computed above the pre-flight. So the one place that turns config mistakes into readable messages is bypassed for this key only.

Fix: validate output_dir where output_base is computed (a string check raising the same ValueError shape package_contexts uses), or compute output_base after the pre-flight. Found while implementing stn-p9a; not fixed there because it is not the manifest.

title: Two concurrent test runs corrupt each other: shared basetemp and one browser image tag
description:
The container tier cannot be run twice at once, and neither collision announces itself as a collision.

MEASURED, both of them, while working several branches in parallel worktrees:

1. --basetemp. Two runs given the same --basetemp delete each other's fixture trees, because pytest rotates that directory at startup. The result was '22 failed, 789 passed, 79 errors', almost all FileNotFoundError on paths under the shared basetemp -- which reads as a catastrophic regression rather than as two runs fighting. Re-running with distinct basetemps was clean.

2. The image tag. pipeline.build_browser_image defaults to tag=BROWSER_IMAGE_TAG, a single fixed name. Every run builds and overwrites that one tag, so a second run can rebuild the image out from under a first that is still using it. Not yet observed failing -- the runs were serialised once this was noticed -- so this half is reasoned from the code rather than measured, and should be confirmed before being fixed.

The default basetemp is already per-run (pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>), so this only bites when someone passes --basetemp explicitly -- which is exactly what stn-7im's workaround tells them to do. The two tickets should be read together.

Fix shape: derive the image tag per run (a session-scoped suffix), and either document that --basetemp must be unique per run or have conftest append a unique component to whatever it is given.
design: Do not simply tell people not to run two suites at once. The suite takes ten minutes, AGENTS.md tells every agent to work in a worktree, and working two branches at once is the normal case that arrangement exists to support.
acceptance_criteria: Two full container-tier runs started concurrently from different worktrees both pass; the browser image tag carries a per-run component; stn-7im's --basetemp workaround does not reintroduce the first collision.
notes:
NOT confirmed by the long run on 2026-09-10, and worth recording so the next reader does not take it as evidence.

A full container-tier run appeared hung on a podman run against localhost/stencil_browser:test while another suite had been running concurrently, which looked like the shared-tag half of this ticket biting. It was not: the run completed clean at 871 passed in 10:02. The apparent stall was tests/test_pdf.py's unresolvable-asset cases, which drive html-to-pdf.js against a deliberately broken page.

So the basetemp half of this ticket remains MEASURED and the image-tag half remains REASONED FROM THE CODE. Do not cite this run as evidence for the second half.
close_reason: Both halves. The basetemp collision (measured) is refused: a run marks its basetemp and a second run owned by a LIVE pytest gets a UsageError naming the cause; a stale marker from a crashed run does not block. The image tag (reasoned from the code) is now per-run, overridable with STENCIL_BROWSER_IMAGE_TAG, and the four helpers resolve it at call time rather than binding a default at import -- the same late-binding mistake caught in conftest's low-space threshold one ticket earlier. Measured that the per-run tag is free: 0.5s to build against the existing tag, 0.6s against a brand-new one, because podman's layer cache keys on the Dockerfile and context rather than the name.

title: Subprocess CLI tests in a worktree silently exercise the main checkout, not the branch
description:
tests/test_cli.py's run_cli invokes [sys.executable, '-m', 'stencil.generate']. The editable install in .venv points at the main checkout, so from a git worktree that subprocess runs MAIN's code while the same file's direct-import tests run the WORKTREE's. One test file, two different copies of stencil under test, with nothing saying so.

Hit for real while fixing stn-w4v: the fix was correct and verified by hand with argparse in isolation, and the new tests kept failing because the subprocess was running unfixed code from main. Installing the worktree into its own venv turned 2 failed into 37 passed with no change to the fix.

The dangerous direction is the opposite one, and it is silent: a change that BREAKS the CLI passes in a worktree, because the subprocess never sees it. Every AGENTS.md workflow says to work in a worktree, so this is the default arrangement rather than an unusual one.

Two candidate fixes:
- have run_cli put the repository root on PYTHONPATH for the subprocess, so it runs the code under test whatever is installed; or
- a session-scoped fixture that asserts the installed distribution resolves to the same tree as the imported stencil package, and skips or fails loudly when it does not.

The second is the one that also catches a stale editable install. Related: the developer .venv here reported distribution version 0.1.0 against a 0.36.0 source until reinstalled, which tests/test_cli.py::test_the_reported_version_is_the_installed_one caught -- that test is the existing, narrower instance of this same idea.
design: Prefer the PYTHONPATH fix for correctness plus the assertion fixture for loudness; neither alone is enough. PYTHONPATH alone leaves a stale install undetected for anything that shells out to the console script rather than -m. The assertion alone makes every worktree run fail until someone builds a per-worktree venv, which is a real cost the repository's own workflow would then pay on every branch.
acceptance_criteria: A subprocess-based CLI test run from a worktree exercises that worktree's code; a deliberate break in generate.py's argument parsing fails tests/test_cli.py when run from a worktree with the venv installed from the main checkout.
close_reason: run_cli sets PYTHONPATH to the tree under test, plus a guard that asks the subprocess where it imported stencil from. Verified by proof rather than assertion: main's checkout has zero occurrences of argparse.SUPPRESS and its installed CLI still shows the stn-w4v bug, yet tests/test_cli.py run from the branch worktree against the MAIN venv passes all 41 tests including the two stn-w4v ones -- which is only possible if the subprocess is executing the branch's code.

title: The decision journal keys three different tickets into one file
description:
Found while flushing stn-k73's journal.

~/.claude/foundry/journals/run-7857ebf5bee1.jsonl holds 307 entries spanning THREE epics:

    epic values in that one file: {None: 183, '(unset)': 76, 'stn-bd3': 23, 'stn-3c9': 18, 'stn-ox1': 7}
    ticket pointers: {'stn-bd3.10': 4, 'stn-3c9.4': 1}

stn-3c9 is stn-38o's epic, worked in a different worktree and a different session; stn-bd3 is older still. They should not share a run id with stn-k73's session, and the run id is supposed to be derived from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID via 'decision-journal run-id --key'.

The visible consequence: 'flush --epic stn-ox1' resolved its create-or-claim target to stn-3c9.4 -- ANOTHER epic's decision ticket -- and refused, because a flush REPLACES the design field and writing there would have destroyed stn-38o's decision log. The refusal is the tool working correctly; the shared journal is the bug. Worked around by creating stn-ox1.5 by hand and passing 'flush --ticket stn-ox1.5'.

Two things to investigate:
- why several sessions resolve to one run id (either run-id's key derivation, or the PreToolUse hook journaling under a key that is not the session's)
- whether 'flush' should scope its create-or-claim to entries matching --epic rather than to the journal's most recent ticket pointer, which is what made another epic's ticket the target

The 183 entries with epic None and 76 with '(unset)' are the same story from the other side: entries recorded before an epic existed cannot be flushed anywhere, which is the failure mode ticket-ship-pr's own Decision Journal Setup section warns about.
notes: Root cause confirmed 2026-09-09: the three epics were three ticket-ship-pr subagents of ONE session, and subagents inherit the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so run-id keyed correctly and they still shared a journal; cmd_flush reads every entry with no epic filter. Fix is being made in foundry as foundry-7g1 (attribution rule: unset entries belong to the most recently claimed epic before them; flush/render/status scope to --epic).
close_reason: Root cause fixed upstream in foundry-7g1 (happy-stl/foundry#30): decision-journal flush/render/status now scope to --epic, and unset entries attribute to the most recently claimed epic. The three mixed logs in this repo were repaired in #99. Nothing in stencil to change.

  - phase: implement · tier 2 · `d-d89c606a` · 2026-09-09T00:41:01Z

title: A global --config before the subcommand is silently ignored
description:
Found by the CodeRabbit gate on stn-k73's PR, and CONFIRMED by running it. PRE-EXISTING.

main() adds --config and --dry-run to the top-level parser AND, via _add_global_opts, to every subparser with the same defaults. argparse applies the subparser's default AFTER the main parser has stored the real value, so the default overwrites it:

    $ stencil --config other.yaml list
    Error: no config file at .../$PWD/.config.yaml      # other.yaml ignored
    $ stencil list --config other.yaml
    Available packages:  hs1 ...                          # works

The BROKEN order is the documented one. generate.py's own module docstring reads:

    stencil [--config <path>] gen [--all] [pkg]

so anyone following the usage string gets the wrong file read, with an error that names a file they did not ask for -- or, worse, a SUCCESSFUL run against the wrong config.

Fix: pass default=argparse.SUPPRESS for the duplicated options in _add_global_opts, so an unsupplied subparser option leaves the main parser's parsed value in place. Needs a test matrix over both argument orders across gen/clean/install/list, which is why it was not folded into stn-k73.

Deliberately NOT fixed in stn-k73: that ticket's approved boundary had three objectives, all about config errors failing closed. 'The CLI reads a different file than the one you named' is a distinct failure, and adding it at the review stage would have grown an operator-approved scope by a fourth objective at the last minute. Related: stn-k73's aggregated error message deliberately names no file BECAUSE --config means the path is not always .config.yaml -- which is only half true until this is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed on the CLI branch and verified with the full container tier: 871 passed. --config/--dry-run before the subcommand are honoured (argparse.SUPPRESS on the subparser copies); a package that fails to render or generates nothing fails the command, with every failing package named together; read_lockfile raises pipeline.VendoredAssetError, deliberately not a ValueError, so a damaged install no longer travels on the config-problem channel -- verified end to end with a corrupted lockfile; and config scalars are capped at 400 characters per problem line, the escaping half having already been done by _safe.

title: A symlinked brand: copies under a name clean cannot see and git tracks
description:
Found by the adversarial code review of stn-k73 (PR for epic stn-ox1), REPRODUCED end to end. PRE-EXISTING; not introduced by that change.

copy_brand_image names the destination '(config_dir / relative).resolve().name' -- .resolve() follows symlinks. get_generated_files names the same file 'Path(brand_image).name', from the raw config string. Two spellings of one rule, and they diverge on a symlink:

    ln -s img/siu-logo-2024.svg logo.svg     # brand: file://logo.svg
    stencil gen --all   ->  out/demo/siu-logo-2024.svg
    get_generated_files ->  ['demo/logo.svg']
    stencil clean --all ->  siu-logo-2024.svg SURVIVES

So the copied logo is absent from the managed .gitignore section and survives clean --all. That is exactly stn-k73's failure mode -- a generated file that is neither ignored nor cleaned -- reached by a different route, which is why it is worth its own ticket rather than a footnote.

Fix: make the destination basename come from ONE place. Cheapest is to stop resolving in copy_brand_image (destination = output_dir / Path(relative).name), so the copied name is always the configured name. If following the symlink is deliberate, brand_problem should return the resolved basename and get_generated_files should use that.

Left out of stn-k73 deliberately: copy_brand_image's destination naming was not in that ticket's objectives, the fix changes an output filename (a compatibility question), and it needs its own test.
close_reason: Fixed in the path-containment change: dir, dest and brand now go through check_config_path, C0 controls join the refused class (after the metacharacter and whitespace checks, so \n and tab keep their more specific messages), and a symlinked brand is copied under the name the config gives it so gen, clean and the managed .gitignore agree. 23 new tests in tests/test_path_containment.py; full suite 883 passed.

title: read_lockfile's ValueError is reported as a broken config
description:
Found by the adversarial code review of stn-k73 (PR for epic stn-ox1), and REPRODUCED against a corrupted vendored file.

pipeline.read_lockfile raises FileNotFoundError when a vendored lockfile is missing (which correctly escapes stencil's config pre-flight as a traceback) and ValueError when it does not end in exactly one newline. get_template_context calls it, so that ValueError is collected by package_contexts and reported as a config problem:

    Error: the config has this problem:
    - browser-package-lock.json must end with exactly one newline; npm writes it that way, ...

    Nothing was generated, removed or written. Fix the config and run again -- and if
    files from an earlier, working config are still on disk, remove that directory by
    hand instead of ...

The config is fine. The real fix is 'python3 scripts/vendor_npm_locks.py'. The message sends the user to edit .config.yaml and to rm -rf a generated directory by hand -- wrong advice for the right failure.

Not fixed in stn-k73 because stencil/pipeline.py was outside that ticket's approved boundary. The clean fix is for read_lockfile to raise a distinct type for 'this install is not vendored correctly' -- the same failure class as the FileNotFoundError two lines above it, so arguably one type for both -- which generate.py's pre-flight then does not catch. A comment in package_contexts records the gap and points here.
close_reason: Fixed on the CLI branch and verified with the full container tier: 871 passed. --config/--dry-run before the subcommand are honoured (argparse.SUPPRESS on the subparser copies); a package that fails to render or generates nothing fails the command, with every failing package named together; read_lockfile raises pipeline.VendoredAssetError, deliberately not a ValueError, so a damaged install no longer travels on the config-problem channel -- verified end to end with a corrupted lockfile; and config scalars are capped at 400 characters per problem line, the escaping half having already been done by _safe.

title: gen --all still exits 0 when a template fails to render or a package has no templates
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). Adjacent to that ticket's fail-open class but NOT closed by it -- stn-k73 closes the config-error path only.

Two paths survive it:
- render_templates re-raises (generate.py ~line 1003) and nothing in main catches it, so a StrictUndefined error is still a raw traceback AND still leaves a half-written package on disk.
- generate_package's 'if not template_defs: print(...); return None' (~line 944) lets the --all loop continue and main return with exit 0.

Both are near-dead in practice today, which is why stn-k73's CHANGELOG bullet is worded 'config errors fail the build' rather than 'a broken package fails the build'. Closing these would make the stronger claim true.
close_reason: Fixed on the CLI branch and verified with the full container tier: 871 passed. --config/--dry-run before the subcommand are honoured (argparse.SUPPRESS on the subparser copies); a package that fails to render or generates nothing fails the command, with every failing package named together; read_lockfile raises pipeline.VendoredAssetError, deliberately not a ValueError, so a damaged install no longer travels on the config-problem channel -- verified end to end with a corrupted lockfile; and config scalars are capped at 400 characters per problem line, the escaping half having already been done by _safe.

title: package 'dir' is never validated yet prefixes every path clean deletes
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). PRE-EXISTING, out of scope there.

package.get('dir', package_id) is never run through check_config_path, yet it prefixes every entry get_generated_files returns -- which is every line of the managed .gitignore section AND every path clean_generated deletes. 'dir: ../..' reaches (output_base / entry).resolve() and deletes outside output_base.

Filed because stn-k73 makes stencil tell a 'the config is checked now' story, and this is the loudest remaining place where it is not. Same fix shape as the brand ticket: check_config_path, or a containment check before deletion.
close_reason: Fixed in the path-containment change: dir, dest and brand now go through check_config_path, C0 controls join the refused class (after the metacharacter and whitespace checks, so \n and tab keep their more specific messages), and a symlinked brand is copied under the name the config gives it so gen, clean and the managed .gitignore agree. 23 new tests in tests/test_path_containment.py; full suite 883 passed.

title: brand is the one config path never checked, and copy_brand_image copies a symlink's target into a handed-over folder
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). PRE-EXISTING and deliberately NOT fixed there -- copy_brand_image's body is outside that ticket's objectives.

Every other configured path goes through check_config_path. `brand` does not. Measured through brand_image_path:

  '../../../../etc/passwd.png'  -> '../../../../etc/passwd.png'
  '/var/root/secret.png'        -> '/var/root/secret.png'
  'file:///etc/hosts.svg'       -> '/etc/hosts.svg'

(config_dir / relative).resolve() with an absolute relative yields the absolute path.

The part that matters is not path traversal but CONTENT. copy_brand_image does shutil.copyfile on the RESOLVED path, so a symlink named logo.png pointing at any readable file copies that file's CONTENT into the generated package -- a folder AGENTS.md says is 'routinely handed to someone as a project of their own'. Only the suffix has to look like an image; the content is never checked. That is a content-exfiltration primitive into a distributed artifact.

Not a privilege boundary (whoever writes .config.yaml can already run anything via pre_build.run when someone runs make) -- but note stencil itself never executes that, so a CI job running only 'stencil gen --dry-run' over a PR branch's config gets no execution today and would get this.

Fix to consider: run brand through check_config_path, or at minimum an is_relative_to(config_dir) containment check on the resolved source.
close_reason: Fixed in the path-containment change: dir, dest and brand now go through check_config_path, C0 controls join the refused class (after the metacharacter and whitespace checks, so \n and tab keep their more specific messages), and a symlinked brand is copied under the name the config gives it so gen, clean and the managed .gitignore agree. 23 new tests in tests/test_path_containment.py; full suite 883 passed.

notes:
## AMENDMENTS from the Phase 4 adversarial review -- additional required cases

1. `install` on a config that ALREADY HAS a managed section. The acceptance
   criterion "no section is written at all" is only true on the CREATE path; on
   the UPDATE path an abort leaves the OLD section intact. Test BOTH paths, and
   assert the old section is unchanged rather than absent.

2. A TYPE-broken package through the CLI, not just a value-broken one:
   `docs: 7` (TypeError), `package_name: 42` on a doc package with sources
   (AttributeError), `output_dir: 5` (TypeError). Each: non-zero, no Traceback.
   A ValueError-only pre-flight passes the "no Traceback" contract by fixture
   selection alone, which is what makes this the test that matters.

3. Control characters in a package id (e.g. `\x1b[1A` or `\r`): the aggregated
   message must not contain a raw ESC or CR. This is what makes the aggregation
   guarantee true of what the reader SEES, not just of the Python string.

4. One config-level typo (a top-level quoted `show_download`) must produce ONE
   line, not one per package -- the dedupe guard.

5. `gen <pkg>` (single package) fails when a DIFFERENT package is broken, and
   `clean <pkg>` likewise. Decision d-adf7c52b: this is deliberate collective
   behaviour, so pin it -- otherwise the next contributor "fixes" it as a bug.

6. `gen` with a dangling brand leaves NO output directory behind
   (`output_base/<pkg_dir>` does not exist afterwards). Stronger and more
   honest than "nothing written": it is the assertion that proves the
   pre-flight ran before `output_dir.mkdir`.

   the .gitignore entry and the clean list derive from the brand string, not the

   brand-alt row (~line 248) needs both halves, not just "stencil gen fails".

   .gitignore section is not written at all rather than written incomplete" is
   only true on the CREATE path. On the UPDATE path an abort leaves the OLD
   section intact -- which is the safe direction (a stale section is a superset
   for every package that was already fine, so it over-ignores; a truncated one
   under-ignores and silently makes a build product committable). Word it as
   "the managed section is never replaced by a truncated one".

title: Implement: aggregated fail-closed pre-flight in generate.py
description:

## AMENDMENTS from the Phase 4 architecture review

**A1 -- validate_config gains config_dir. This is the fix for a hole in the
original plan, not a refinement.** Without it objective 3 is unmet for `gen`,
the command it was written about: the pre-flight would run brand_problem with
no filesystem root, skip the existence half, let render_templates write every
file, and then copy_brand_image (line 952, OUTSIDE generate_package's try)
throws a raw traceback over a half-generated directory -- verbatim the defect
objective 3 exists to close.

    validate_config(config: dict, env: Environment, config_dir: Path | None = None)

passes config_dir through to the pre-flight; main line ~1342 becomes
`validate_config(config, env, config_dir)`, where config_dir is already in
scope (line ~1287). tests/test_config_validation.py:43 calls it with two
positional args, so the optional third is safe.

**A2 -- the existence check is gen-only. get_generated_files,
install_gitignore and clean_generated gain NOTHING; leave all three
signatures exactly as they are.** This REPLACES plan step 5. Reason recorded
as decision d-96da97d8: the .gitignore entry and the clean list both derive
from the brand STRING (line ~1055), not from the file, so a missing brand file
cannot make either list short -- the check buys install and clean no
fail-closed value and only adds a way for `clean`, a recovery operation, to
refuse. The rule to write into the comment: fail closed on what the config
SAYS (deterministic, machine-independent); check what the filesystem HAS only
where stencil is about to depend on it.

install and clean still fail closed on every config error, including a missing
brand-alt. Only the file-existence half is gen-only.

**A3 -- collect more than ValueError, and guard the shapes.** get_template_context
line ~201 does `config.get("packages", {}).get(package_id)` and line ~205 does
`package.get(...)`, so `packages:` as a LIST and a package whose value is a
STRING both raise AttributeError, not ValueError -- a raw traceback from
exactly the malformed config this pre-flight exists to report. Also `docs: 5`
(TypeError), `output_dir: 5` (TypeError), `brand: 5` (AttributeError).

  (a) Reject a non-mapping config["packages"], and a non-mapping package value,
      with a clear ValueError naming the offender. load_config (line ~60) sets
      the precedent for the message style.
  (b) Collect `(ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError, KeyError)` and include
      `type(e).__name__` in the collected line, so a genuine stencil bug stays
      distinguishable from a config error rather than being laundered into one.

  Do NOT catch bare Exception: pipeline.read_lockfile raises
  FileNotFoundError/ValueError for a broken INSTALL, and that must not be
  reported as a config error in every package at once.

**A4 -- gate brand_problem on has_pages.** copy_brand_image is called only under
`if context.get("has_pages")` (line ~950) and get_generated_files gates its
brand entry the same way (line ~1052). Ungated, a page-less package
(package_type: none, no docs/slides) inheriting a config-level image brand with
no brand-alt would NEWLY fail gen/install/clean -- and because config-level
brands are inherited, one missing brand-alt at the top level would name every
page-less package at once. Call brand_problem only when the just-computed
context["has_pages"] is true; the context is right there, so this costs nothing.

**A5 -- define the both-broken interaction.** When get_template_context raised
for a package: record that message and `continue`. Do NOT then call
brand_problem for it -- there is no context to read has_pages from, and a
non-mapping package value would explode inside the collector itself.

**A6 -- preserve the two message substrings.** brand_problem's returned strings
must keep the literal substrings `brand-alt` and `not a file`:
tests/test_brand.py's `pytest.raises(match=...)` regexes are substring
searches, and those two tests are what prove copy_brand_image still raises for
the direct generate_package API that conftest.make_package uses. Preserve
copy_brand_image's early short-circuit too -- brand_image_path() returning None
means return None BEFORE the alt check, so a plain-name brand and a remote URL
are still fine with no alt.

**A7 -- move the stale comment.** The aggregation rationale at lines ~706-708
("a config error in one should not hide a naming error in another") is the
reason the pre-flight aggregates; move it onto the new function. Update
validate_config's docstring, which will no longer describe what it does.

## AMENDMENTS from the Phase 4 adversarial review (second pass)

**B1 -- keep main's `try` NARROW. Do not wrap the whole install/clean branch.**
This REPLACES the wording of plan step 6. `clean_generated` unlinks files in a
loop and then rmdirs; a broad `except ValueError` there would print a bare
`Error: <msg>` with the traceback suppressed AFTER an unknown number of files
were already deleted. Suppressing a traceback is right for "your config is
wrong" and WRONG for "something failed halfway through destroying files". The
gen branch already does this correctly -- its try at line ~1338 wraps
`validate_config(config, env)` and nothing else. Mirror that: call the
validation explicitly and narrowly, catch around THAT call only, then run
install_gitignore / clean_generated outside the try.

**B2 -- escape control characters in the aggregated message.** The interpolations
in generate.py are raw, no `!r`: `{package_id}` everywhere, `{package_type}`
(:220), `{package['package_folder']}` (:236), brand `{value}` (:795, :806),
`{', '.join(clashes)}` (:545). A package id or brand value containing `\r` or
`\x1b[1A\x1b[2K` erases previously-printed lines of the report -- defeating
the exact "one error cannot hide another" guarantee this PR sells, while the
aggregation test still passes because it asserts on the Python string and the
terminal renders something else. Also a CI-log integrity issue. Escape each
collected problem as it goes into the aggregate:

    def _safe(text: str) -> str:
        """Config-supplied text is data, not terminal control."""
        return "".join(
            c if c == "\n" or c == " " or c.isprintable() else repr(c)[1:-1]
            for c in str(text)
        )

Note `check_config_path` and `show_download_default` already use `{text!r}` /
`{value!r}` and are safe -- do not change them.

**B3 -- dedupe identical problems.** `show_download_default` checks package scope
then CONFIG scope and raises with where="config"; `reject_derived("config-level",
...)` runs inside every package's context build; a config-level brand with no
brand-alt fails for every package via brand_of's fallback. So ONE top-level typo
produces one identical line per package -- 200 packages, 200 identical lines,
and the real per-package errors scroll off. Dedupe the collected strings
(`dict.fromkeys` preserves order) before building the message.

**B4 -- brand_problem's config_dir must be positional-required.** An optional
`config_dir=None` that silently skips half the check is the same shape of defect
this PR removes: three call sites must remember to pass it and forgetting is
silent. Make it `brand_problem(package, config, config_dir)` -- callers with no
root pass an explicit `None`. The PUBLIC get_generated_files /
install_gitignore / clean_generated params stay optional-and-last for the
positional call sites in tests; that part is unaffected (and per d-96da97d8
those three gain no parameter at all).

**B5 -- get_generated_files must CONSUME the returned contexts.** It must not
call the pre-flight and then keep its own get_template_context loop -- that
would take install/clean from N context builds to 2N. Consuming them is the
only reason the pre-flight returns them.

**B6 -- reorder clean's unknown-package check.** After this change
`clean <unknown-pkg>` on a config that ALSO has a broken package reports the
config error instead of "Unknown package", because get_generated_files
(line ~1093) now precedes the membership check (line ~1099). Move the
membership check ahead of the entries computation.

**B7 -- the error message names the escape hatch.** `clean` becomes unavailable
exactly when it is most wanted: config drifted, generated files on disk. Failing
closed is still right (deleting from a misread config is worse), but the message
must say the way out -- fix the config, or remove the directory by hand --
or the first person to hit it reaches for a wider `rm -rf` than they meant.

**B8 -- collective failure is DECIDED (d-adf7c52b): every command, all packages.**
`gen <pkg>` and `clean <pkg>` fail when a DIFFERENT package is broken. This is
deliberate, not a side effect: validate_config already gates single-package gen
on global template_env/when: errors today, so this extends an existing contract
rather than inventing one. Document it in STENCIL.md (stn-ox1.3) and pin it with
a test (stn-ox1.4).

**B9 -- correct the aggregation justification, do not repeat mine.** My plan
claimed the line-706 comment's intent "survives the move to failing closed".
That is only half true and the comment must not say otherwise: aggregation
preserves it WITHIN the class of package errors, but the `when:` and unread
`template_env` checks now sit BEHIND the pre-flight and are deferred by one
round. That is deliberate -- you cannot report "Known keys:" from a config you
cannot read, and today's answer is computed from a silently truncated set --
but write it honestly on the new function rather than claiming nothing was lost.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed. Four corrections in review: a misattribution bug that blamed a valid package for a malformed sibling (shape now checked in its own pass, since get_template_context reads every package via declared_template_env_keys); dropped the 'ValueError: ' prefix from ordinary config messages, keeping class names only on unexpected types where they mean something; rewrote the lead line, which read 'Error: Config is broken:' and named .config.yaml even under --config; and switched main's pre-flight from get_generated_files to package_contexts so the call says what it is for. 803 passed before rebase, 849 after.

title: Pin pandoc's YAML boolean resolution in a test
description:
Write tests/test_yaml_resolution.py (NEW FILE).

Files: tests/test_yaml_resolution.py

An integration-marked module that OWNS the measurement three prose sites
currently restate from memory. It writes a probe Lua filter and a front matter
block covering every spelling, drives them through pipeline.PANDOC_IMAGE
directly (NOT pipeline.render -- its argv is fixed and runs the whole template
chain), and asserts the measured table.

REUSE pipeline.container_runtime() and pipeline.PANDOC_IMAGE. Do not invent a
third way to find docker/podman. pipeline.py itself is on the deny list, so the
few lines of docker-run argv are duplicated deliberately rather than by
refactoring the render harness.

MEASURED against pandoc 3.10.0.0 -- pandoc resolves exactly YAML 1.1's
ENUMERATED boolean forms, which means three casings and no others:

  boolean:      y Y yes Yes YES  n N no No NO
                on On ON  off Off OFF
                true True TRUE  false False FALSE
  MetaString '': null Null NULL, ~, and a blank value (all indistinguishable)
  nil:          the key absent
  MetaInlines:  EVERYTHING ELSE, including
                  - mixed case: nO yEs yeS ofF oN tRue falsE nUll
                  - numbers and words: 1 0 2 none
                  - anything quoted: "no" "null" ""

'(any case)' IS WRONG and must not be repeated -- it is one of the claims this
ticket exists to correct. Stencil still behaves correctly for mixed case only
because truthy() lowercases before consulting the FALSE table, which is a
better reason for that table to exist than the ticket gives.

The probe reports type(v), pandoc.utils.type(v) and pandoc.utils.stringify(v)
per key, prints a marker-prefixed JSON line, and the test json.loads it -- the
shape tests/test_download.py uses for its browser probe.

NOTE: this is a characterization pin, not a red-green test. It passes on the
first run because pandoc already behaves this way; its job is to FAIL on a
future image bump that flips resolution. Say that in the docstring rather than
pretending it drove the implementation.

Acceptance: passes under a real pandoc container; a deliberately wrong expected
value fails with a message naming the key and the type; the module cannot pass
by measuring nothing.
close_reason: tests/test_yaml_resolution.py pins all 43 spellings; both mutations independently reproduced

title: Write tests: disk-naming hook behaviour
description:
The coverage the epic's test strategy promises for the disk-naming hooks, which no other task authors. Architecture review found this gap: stn-0ot.3 would otherwise land with no red test, while stn-0ot.2 gets one.

Files: tests/test_tmp_footprint.py

Exercise the free-space helper and the pytest_runtest_makereport annotation path against a SYNTHETIC report and an injected threshold -- never by actually filling a disk, and never needing a container runtime.

Assert:
1. The helper returns a message naming the basetemp path and the free bytes when free space is below the threshold, and returns None above it.
2. The annotation reaches a FAILING report's sections when space is low.
3. A PASSING report is left untouched, and a failing report with plenty of free space is left untouched -- an annotation on every failure would be noise that trains people to ignore it.
4. The helper survives a basetemp path that has been removed, returning None rather than raising. A hook that raises would turn an ordinary test failure into a confusing internal error, which is the opposite of this feature's purpose.

title: Implement: name the disk when the tier fails
description:
Make a disk-exhaustion failure say so, instead of the plain exit 1 stn-7im describes.

Files: tests/conftest.py

Two hooks plus one small shared helper that returns free space on the filesystem holding the basetemp:

- pytest_report_header: print the basetemp path and the free space on its filesystem, every run. The point is that the number is in the log of the run that failed, not only in a postmortem someone thinks to do.
- pytest_runtest_makereport: when a test FAILS and free space on the basetemp filesystem is below a threshold, attach a report section naming the basetemp path, the free bytes, and the --basetemp workaround. It has to be caught at the moment of failure: with retention=failed, passing tests free their trees as they go, so by terminal-summary time the disk can look healthy after having been exhausted mid-run. Use @pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True) -- pyproject requires pytest>=8.0, where that is the current spelling.

Pick a threshold that is defensible and state the reasoning in a comment: below it, the disk is a plausible cause of an arbitrary failure; above it, it is not. A generated package is 10.75MB and a container build needs headroom.

Both hooks must be robust: shutil.disk_usage on a path that has gone away must not turn a test failure into a collection error. Neither hook may import anything requiring a container runtime.

Acceptance: the header line appears in a normal run naming the basetemp and its free space; the unit tier still passes; no new failure is introduced when disk space is plentiful.
close_reason: Hooks implemented in tests/conftest.py: pytest_report_header names the basetemp and its free space every run, and a wrapper pytest_runtest_makereport annotates a FAILING test when space is low -- at the moment of failure, because with retention=failed a run that exhausted the disk looks healthy by summary time. Tested by driving the real hook, which found the threshold was bound at import.

title: Document the retention trade in AGENTS.md
description:

Cover: the measurement (10.75MB per generated package, 823MB of retained basetemp for the unit tier alone, 3 runs kept, a 7.7GB tmpfs); that the fix is retention rather than package size; the cost being accepted (a passing test's output is gone) and the override that buys it back (-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all); and that the ticket's other candidate -- sharing one generated package -- was deliberately left to stn-vda because it is a wall-clock change, not a disk one.

title: Write tests: basetemp footprint guard
description:
Write tests/test_tmp_footprint.py, the guard stn-7im's design field asks for.

Files: tests/test_tmp_footprint.py (new)

Two guards, both measuring the BASETEMP TREE rather than /tmp -- the design note is explicit that a guard reading /tmp passes on a big tmpfs and fails on a small one, which is nobody's useful signal:

1. Behavioral retention guard. Run an inner pytest as a subprocess (precedent: tests/test_cli.py runs the CLI as a subprocess, with its reasoning in a docstring there) over a generated throwaway test module, with its own --basetemp under tmp_path. Assert a PASSING inner test leaves nothing behind, and a FAILING inner test keeps its tree. This proves the mechanism rather than restating the config string -- AGENTS.md records that a guard which silently stops running is worse than no guard, and that is exactly what asserting on getini() would be.
2. Per-package size cap. Generate one package into tmp_path via the existing make_package/generate_package path and assert its total size is under a cap. Today it is 10.75MB (html-template.html 5.30MB + slide-template.html 5.32MB). Pick a cap with headroom for ordinary growth that still catches a doubling; state the current measurement in a comment so the next reader knows what the cap is protecting.

Neither test may be marked integration -- they must run without a container runtime.

Acceptance: the file parses and collects; the behavioral guard FAILS before the pyproject setting lands (a passing inner test's tree is still retained) and the size cap passes. This is the TDD red phase.

REVISION (architecture review). The inner pytest invocation must read THIS REPOSITORY'S real configuration, and the task previously left the mechanism unspecified. Both easy implementations are wrong: a throwaway module under tmp_path has no pyproject.toml in its ancestry, so plain discovery falls back to pytest's built-in default and the guard stays red forever; and hardcoding -o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed in the inner run makes it tautological -- it would verify pytest's feature works, passing identically before and after stn-0ot.2, which is precisely the TDD signal this task exists to provide.

Use: python3 -m pytest <throwaway>.py -c <repo_root>/pyproject.toml --basetemp=<tmp_path>/bt -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:randomly

This has been validated empirically against the current tree: with the repo's config as it stands today it retains BOTH test trees, and with -o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed added it retains ONLY the failing test's. The run costs 0.14s. Two facts that follow and that the assertion must respect: the throwaway module holds one passing and one failing test so a SINGLE inner run proves the discrimination rather than two runs proving two independent facts; and pytest writes <name>current SYMLINKS beside the real directories, so the assertion must filter to real directories or it will read a symlink as a retained tree.

Locate the repo root from __file__ rather than cwd -- the test must not depend on where pytest was invoked from.

title: The container tier fills a 7.7GB /tmp and fails spuriously
description:
A full `pytest` run exhausted a 7.7GB tmpfs /tmp on this machine, and the failure did not look like a disk failure: two runs reported plain exit 1, and the harness capturing their output hit ENOSPC of its own. Clearing /tmp/pytest-of-wgrim took /tmp from 100% to 2%, so the tier's own temp dirs were the whole of it.

Each generated package carries html-template.html at 5.3MB -- the inlined Bootstrap, highlight.js, Mermaid and fonts -- and the tier does a fresh `stencil gen` per test, so the basetemp tree grows by megabytes per test and pytest keeps the last three runs. Add the PDFs the pandoc and browser services write and a full run does not fit on a default Fedora tmpfs.

Workaround while this is open: `pytest --basetemp=~/.cache/stencil-pytest` puts the tree on disk instead.

Two candidate fixes, neither obviously right yet: have the tier's fixtures share one generated package where a test does not need its own (stn-vda is the same underlying cost, from the wall-clock side), or stop writing the 5.3MB template into every generated package under test by pointing the fixture at a cached copy. Either way the tier should also fail with something that names the disk.
design: Worth a test only if a cheap one exists -- a guard that asserts the suite's own footprint is bounded would have caught this, but it has to measure the basetemp tree rather than /tmp, or it fails on whoever's machine has a big tmpfs and passes on nobody's.
close_reason: Shipped and measured. tmp_path_retention_policy=failed, plus a report header naming the basetemp and its free space and a low-space annotation on failing tests at the moment of failure. Same full container-tier run before and after: the basetemp tree went from 4.0GB to 117MB, a 34x reduction, 872 passed either way. The retention guard is behavioural -- an inner pytest run against this repository's own pyproject.toml -- and was verified by removing the setting and watching it red. AGENTS.md records the trade, the override, and why stn-vda (wall-clock) and stn-zim (concurrency) are separate problems.
